notes.title: V1.0.2 is back
notes.notes:
After doing some more internal testing on v1.0.2 we couldn't reproduce the issue that prompted the rollback to 1.0.1.

Since 1.0.2 corrects a blocking bug for steam deck users, we opted to reinstate it.

We think the issue reported to us was an isolated incident, but please if you do have an issue, don't hesitate to report it on our [url=https://discord.gg/kns824Mekj]discord server[/url]

notes.title: Temporary rollback to v1.0.1
notes.notes:
Hey fellow Asfalians,
we've discovered a game breaking bug in our latest 1.0.2 update, so in order to take our time to review this and make a proper fix, we're rolling back the game to v1.0.1 which doesn't have that bug.

We hope to fix this rapidly early next week.

Thanks for your understanding and apoligies to those who might have encountered the bugs.

notes.title: Update 1.0.2 Patch notes
notes.notes:
[h2]Heya fellow Asfalians,[/h2]

Asfalia: Fear was released two weeks ago and we've received a lot of positive feedback so before anything, a great big "thank you" for taking part in this great adventure within Charlie's world of emotions.

We've done our best to bring you a game without bugs, but our best wasn't enough and some of those cheesy vilains managed to sneak through the gaps. Fortunately, we've been watching many streams and looking at comments from reviewers and on our discord server, and we've been paying attention.

[h2]So what's been fixed exactly in this update:[/h2]

[list]
[*] Kniferatu no longer takes all the attention to himself when you go back to the crypt from the Isle of Greywing. He might have something to say, but at least he won't block the game in doing so.
[*] In some specific cases it was possible to fix the drone in Echo Town twice, resulting in an incorrect chip count and an empty 6th drone. Media asked Pi to spin some solution, and he did come around and solved this pesky issue.
[*] If you have a controller plugged in, and start playing ghost invaders, you will no longer lose control of your ship.
[*] The speed of the cursor in Lily's minigame no longer approaches lightspeed in some circumstances. And we also added a dynamic difficulty adjustment that kicks in after a few seconds, so it's never too difficult to beat it.
[*] It's no longer possible to get the speedrun achievement in the forest just by going back to the playground after Charlie arrives.
[/list]

[h2]New features are brewing[/h2]

We've had some requests for some much needed features and we agree that they are important. We're working on them, and we'll also make sure they're properly validated before we release them, so please bare with us. But it's coming in a not far future.

[list]
[*][b] Controller support: [/b]we're still in the process of figuring out the right approach for controller support, but we've found some promissing answers to this complicated puzzle.

[*][b]New languages: [/b]The whole game is being translated (text only) to Brasilian, Japanese, German, Spanish and Russian. We have to validate the translations but it's nearing completion.

[*][b]Windowed mode: [/b]Ultra wide screen users, muti screen users, streamers, we heard you. Windowed mode is coming !

[*][b]Photosensitive option: [/b]Some players like to play in the dark, and those big flashes can be painful. Even more so if you have photosensitive epilepsy. We're adding a feature to turn white flashes into black flashes.
[/list]

[h2]Did we forget something?[/h2]
We're doing our best to do what needs to be done, but if your feedback is the best food for change. One could even say, it's delicious!

So don't hesitate to let us know with a review or by popping by on our discord server.

notes.title: Privacy Update and Bugfix
notes.notes:
[h1]Privacy Update[/h1]
[h2]Understanding our Players[/h2]
In an effort to better understand how players interact with the game, we've added analytics to the game. Basically what this does is send us statistics of what players do when playing the game. We track simple things like what language players choose, when they reach certain milestones in the game or interact with the environment.

That sort of data helps us understand if the players' experience corresponds to our expectations, and if it doesn't, we can adjust things to improve that experience.

[h2]Anonymous Data[/h2]
The data we receive is anonymous, we cannot trace it back to you, it is associated to an ID that allows us to distinguish one player from another, but that ID is all we have.

Below is a sample event from a user who finished playing a minigame. All we know is the score obtained, and some very restricted information about their operating system (Windows PC) and country (US)

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44256832/f7d782dc620c187760227b3eaffe4c3602b68c4d.png[/img]

Even though that data is anonymous, it is still considered private data.

[h2]Who has access to this data?[/h2]
Statistical data is sent only to Unity, which is the service provider that enables us to process this data. It is not shared, either by us or by Unity, with any other supplier.

[h2]Your Privacy Matters![/h2]
We owe the players full transparency, and full control over their data.

When you start the game for the first time, we'll ask for your consent, and at any point you can change your opinion by going into the options menu. There you can also erase any personal data you've sent in the past.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44256832/e215d46f5b75a777e87bc590381ebcc3b7432b77.png[/img]

[h1]Bug Fixes[/h1]
- Fixed a bug where sometimes the pumpking wouldn't give you the key and you'd have to start a new game to get past.
